newsitem.title: CHINA: China says 1989 crackdown raised to hurt U.S. ties.
newsitem.headline: China says 1989 crackdown raised to hurt U.S. ties.

text.p: China said on Thursday that renewed criticism by some Americans of Beijing's 1989 crackdown on dissent was designed to prevent an improvement in Sino-U.S. ties.

"There are some people in the United States who bring this issue up and I think their reason is they don't want to see an improvement and development in Sino-U.S. ties," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang.
"This question is so far in the past. We have already reached a conclusion on this," he told reporters at a regular news briefing.

A U.S. House Human Rights Subcommittee hearing was held in Washington on Wednesday to challenge a statement made last week by Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian on his U.S. visit that no one was killed at Beijing's Tiananmen Square when Chinese troops crushed the protests.
Hundreds of people were killed in Beijing during the crackdown by the army.
Beijing has admitted to some deaths but it prefers to say only that no one died inside Beijing's Tiananmen Square, the centre of the protests and a symbol of Communist rule.
Louisa Coan of Amnesty International USA said China has refused to allow outside investigators to determine if people were killed in Tiananmen Square itself.
